title: ork wait: do not fire again on a run whose question is answered and that only waits for a slot under the global cap

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
On 2026-11-26, after `ork answer ork-20261126-021911-97a7 ...` (S618) returned "resume waits for a slot; it starts before queued runs", the run showed "paused ... (wait: resume waits for a slot under global cap 4)". Every new `ork wait --project ork --until question,stopped,landed`, and even `--until stopped,landed`, then exited at once with "ork-20261126-021911-97a7 S618 question key: base-overlays.tracking-paths next: ork answer ...". The question was already answered. The orchestrator could only watch landings until a slot freed, which hides real stops and new questions.

The cause is `judge` in `internal/cli/wait.go`. It reads the run only from `run.show`, where an answered run that waits for a slot is still `paused` with `pending.kind` `question` (`questionPending`, `internal/cli/wait.go:155`). `run.show` does not say the run waits for a slot. The daemon's status does: `EngineRun.ResumeWaiting` (`internal/source/source.go:410`). The TUI and `status` already file such a run under Running (`internal/source/source.go:502`).

Owner decision (adj 613, `wait.resume-waiting-source`, `status-call`): read `ResumeWaiting` from the status call, with no wire change. `ork wait` then treats a run that waits only for a slot as in progress. It is not a question, a stop or an `--until` match. Once the run starts, or asks again, the wait reads it as before.

Owner decision, 2026-11-27 (adj 613): ork wait reads ResumeWaiting from the status call it already makes; no wire change.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
All tests are in `internal/cli/wait_test.go`, using `waitFake.handle`, `multiFake`, and `runQuestion`. The first two and the new-question transition fail on current code. The unchanged-question guard intentionally passes before the change.
- TestWaitSlotWaitingQuestionIsNotAStop: one named run reads a paused question with status ResumeWaiting true, then implement, then landed. For both --until question,stopped,landed and --until paused,stopped,landed, exit 0 with exactly r1 landed and at least three run.show reads.
- TestWaitProjectSkipsASlotWaitingQuestion: --project p --until question,landed follows slot-waiting r1 and r2 going implement then landed. Exit 0 with exactly r2 S2 landed; r1 is not printed.
- TestWaitQuestionStillStopsWhenTheRunDoesNotWaitForASlot: the same question with no ResumeWaiting status entry exits ExitWaitQuestion (3) and prints the question.
- TestWaitSlotWaitingRunStopsOnANewQuestion: the first question has ResumeWaiting true; a later new question has it false. Exit 3 with the new question.
The fake gets a slotWait set; MethodStatus lists those ids as paused pending question with ResumeWaiting true, including for an empty Project. Status changes for the new-question test occur under the fake mutex based on run.show reads.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In `internal/cli/wait.go`, add `slotWait bool` to `followed`, with the comment "the status call says the run waits for a slot (adj 613)".
2. Add a method on `waiter`, `slotWaiting(ctx, c *daemon.Client, id string) (bool, error)`. It calls `daemon.MethodStatus` with `daemon.StatusParams{Project: w.project}`. An empty `w.project` asks for every project, which the daemon allows (`internal/daemon/handlers.go:391-414`). It returns true when an `EngineRun` with that `ID` and `ResumeWaiting` true is in `res.Projects[*].EngineRuns`. A run that is not listed gives false.
3. In the read loop of `connection` (`internal/cli/wait.go:238-257`), after a successful `c.Show` and before `w.judge`, set `f.slotWait = false`. When `questionPending(reply)` is true, call `w.slotWaiting` once for that run and store the result. Make no status call for a read that is not a pending question. A failed call goes through `drop(err)` like a failed `Show`.
4. In `judge`, keep the base, `last` and ended-rounds bookkeeping, then add `case f.slotWait && questionPending(r): return verdictNone`, first in the `switch` and before the `--until` cases. The run is in progress, so neither `question`, `paused`, `stopped` nor `landed` matches it, and the `--stage` check is not reached.
5. Update the comment above `judge`: a pending question ends the wait unless the status call says the run only waits for a slot.
6. Update `docs/guide.md:730`: a pending question ends the wait with code 3, except a question the owner answered whose run only waits for a slot under the global cap. That run counts as in progress. Update `docs/state.md:1001-1002` the same way for the `question` and `paused` names.
7. Add the four tests and the `slotWait` field with its status handling in `internal/cli/wait_test.go`.
8. Write the changelog entry with `slicer changelog add S621 --text "..."`, and do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- Acceptance: an answered run that waits for a slot does not end ork wait with a question line, whatever --until lists.
- Acceptance: a pending question on a run that does not wait for a slot still ends the wait with exit 3.
- Acceptance: when the run asks again or starts, the wait reads it as before.
- Acceptance: no wire change; internal/daemon and internal/source are untouched.
- `go test -run TestWaitSlotWaitingQuestionIsNotAStop ./internal/cli` passes.
- `go test -run TestWaitProjectSkipsASlotWaitingQuestion ./internal/cli` passes.
- `go test -run TestWaitQuestionStillStopsWhenTheRunDoesNotWaitForASlot ./internal/cli` passes.
- `go test -run TestWaitSlotWaitingRunStopsOnANewQuestion ./internal/cli` passes.
- `go test ./internal/cli` passes, with the existing wait tests unchanged.
- `go test ./...` passes.
- `go vet ./...` prints nothing.
- `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
- `slicer check` reports no problem.
